raw: Injury Report Home   >   2026 Ultimate Draft Kit   >  UDK – Injury Report Recap of the health and recovery from major injuries QB RB WR TE Patrick Mahomes KC | 30 Years Old ACL + LCL Surgery Date: December 15, 2025 Return Timeline: Limited throughout the offseason, Likely ready for Week 1 Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs had a disappointing 2025 season by their standards, and it all culminated in Week 15 when the All-Pro QB tore two ligaments in his left knee. Mahomes tore the ACL and the LCL (ligament on the outside of the knee) in mid-December and was placed on IR. Generally speaking, players off an isolated ACL injury wait about four weeks to have surgery in order to allow swelling to come down and restore knee range of motion, but Mahomes' procedure was performed the day after his injury in order to repair the LCL right away. This multi-ligament procedure comes with a lengthy rehab process that will extend well into the summer. However, because Mahomes is a QB and can play from the pocket, I do think he has a chance to be ready for the start of the regular season. If he were an RB, WR, or TE, he would certainly be starting on PUP. When Mahomes does get back on the field, fantasy gamers should not expect any of the rushing production we saw in 2025 when he set career highs in per-game rushing attempts, yards, and TDs. He will be a strict pocket passer for the majority of the 2026 season. Bo Nix DEN | 26 Years Old Right Ankle Fracture Surgery Date: January 20, 2026 Return Timeline: Cleared for Training Camp, Ready for Week 1 Nix injured his right ankle late in the team's win over the Bills in the Divisional Round of the playoffs and underwent surgery a few days later to address a fracture. It remains unclear whether Nix is dealing with a joint-related issue stemming from previous ankle injuries or another structural problem. Nix has a significant ankle injury history dating back to his college days, and head coach Sean Payton alluded to it when discussing Nix's recent procedure. Right now, the details of the injury aren't known, but reports from late April indicated that the Denver QB required a follow up procedure on the ankle. This isn't necessarily unusual, but it does add a layer of complexity to his injury and his injury history. Sometimes a second minor procedure is required to remove hardware, or a "clean up" procedure is used to address joint stiffness. Either way, this doesn't change his season-long outlook for 2026. Nix has been fully cleared for training camp and will be ready to go for Week 1 barring any unforeseen setbacks. Daniel Jones IND | 29 Years Old Achilles Surgery Date: December 9, 2025 Return Timeline: Cleared for Week 1 Jones and the Colts caught the league by storm in 2025 and looked like they were headed for a top seed in the AFC. Sadly, that all came to an abrupt end when Jones tore the Achilles in his right leg in Week 14 against Jacksonville. Jones underwent surgery in early December, so he spent the early part of the offseason and summer rehabbing. I do expect him to return to the field early in training camp, though he will not be 100%. He's very likely to be cleared for Week 1, but his status is worth monitoring throughout August. The reason he has a chance to return within about nine months is because of the position he plays. If he were an RB or WR, there is no chance he would be able to play in nine months, but given that he is a QB, he can play his position at less than 100%. Now, that does not mean we're going to be getting pre-injury Daniel Jones in the first chunk of the season. His mobility, especially as a runner, is going to be compromised for the vast majority of the 2026 season. Furthermore, because this is Jones' right leg, and he's a right-handed QB, his push off that right leg during dropbacks could be negatively impacted, thereby reducing his downfield velocity and accuracy. Michael Penix Jr. ATL | 26 Years Old ACL Surgery Date: Week of November 24, 2025 Return Timeline: Limited throughout the offseason, Could be ready for Week 1 Coming into the NFL, Penix had a lengthy and somewhat concerning injury history. He had multiple ACL injuries in his right knee in college, and those knee concerns have not gone away in the pros. Penix missed a game in Week 8 because of a bone bruise in his knee, and then suffered a season-ending left knee injury in Week 11 when he suffered a partially torn ACL. Sometimes, players can function with a partial tear of the major ligament, but ultimately, the medical staff and team opted for a full reconstruction, suggesting the injury was more severe than just a minor sprain. With Penix's surgery taking place in late November, he will have roughly eight months of rehab before training camp and about nine months before the start of the season. Therefore, he will be doing limited work with the offense in OTAs and minicamp, but I do expect him to ramp up his participation during training camp. Given that Penix is a pure pocket passer, he does have a good chance to be ready for Week 1 in a vacuum. The reason I put it that way is that this is not a "normal situation" by any means. The QB now has a significant injury history on both knees, and the Falcons invested the 8th overall pick in him just a couple of years ago. They will surely want to give him every chance to be their long-term starter moving forward, but if they rush him back, the chances of him developing into the franchise QB could be compromised. Given his injury history, it would not be surprising to see the team take a more conservative approach, so for now, I'd consider him questionable for Week 1. Ashton Jeanty LV | 22 Years Old Right Ankle Sprain Return Timeline: Situation to Monitor; Questionable for Week 1 Las Vegas' star RB left practice on Sunday, August 23 with a right ankle injury and did not return. Multiple local beat reports indicated that Jeanty collided with a teammate while attempting to catch a pass, and following the play, he was unable to put any weight on his right leg as he was assisted off the field with trainers. Initially, there was fear Jeanty might miss a significant amount of time, but following additional testing and evaluation, it now appears this is not a long-term injury. Without video or details from the team, it's difficult to provide any specific analysis. If this a mild-to-moderate sprain, Jeanty could be back within the first couple of weeks of the season, but if this on the more severe side, he could be sidelined for some regular season games. Jeremiyah Love ARI | 21 Years Old Left High Ankle Sprain Return Timeline: Questionable for Week 1 The #3 overall pick in the NFL Draft is now dealing with an ankle injury after he exited the Cardinals' first preseason game on August 13. Initially, Mike LaFleur downplayed the injury, stating that Jeremiyah Love would likely return to practice in the near future, but he has since backtracked on that prognosis with the team now confirming that they will hold him out of practice the week of August 17. While the team has not confirmed the specific type of injury, video of the injury is consistent with a high ankle sprain. Furthermore, LaFleur stating that Love came into the building more sore in the days following the injury is consistent with how high ankle sprains tend to behave. Players often feel worse 24 to 48 hours following the injury once swelling and stiffness set in. Right now, fantasy managers shouldn't panic on Love's outlook, especially with four weeks of recovery prior to Week 1. However, it's realistic that the former Notre Dame RB misses multiple weeks in camp, which could affect his early-season playing time and usage. Breece Hall NYJ | 25 Years Old Groin Strain Return Timeline: Like out of practice 1-2 weeks; Questionable for Week 1 Breece Hall left practice on Monday, August 17 with a groin injury and did not return. The coaching staff and local beat reporters confirmed that Hall did receive an MRI and by their accounts, the injury is considered "minor." That could suggest a Grade I strain, which typically only carries a recovery of 1-2 weeks. While that is a reasonable prognosis, it's important to note that the groin muscles are particularly important for running backs because of the constant cutting and change of direction required of the position. Because of that, he could be limited or out of practice for longer than that 1-2 week period. For now, it's not a guarantee that Hall is available for Week 1 until we see him back on the practice field in a couple of weeks. Zach Charbonnet SEA | 25 Years Old ACL Surgery Date: February 20, 2026 Return Timeline: Could begin regular season on PUP Charbonnet tore his ACL in his left knee in the Divisional Round of the playoffs against the 49ers, which was brutal timing for multiple reasons. First, the man didn't get to chase his dreams and play in the Super Bowl, and second, his 2026 outlook is now affected in a major way. Because of this January injury, Charbonnet is going to be limited the entire offseason, including training camp. As of this writing in early February, the specifics of this ACL injury aren't known. For his 2026 return timeline, it matters whether or not this was a clean ACL tear or one that included additional damage. Either way, I expect him to begin the regular season on PUP with the possibility that his recovery extends well into October, depending on the details of the injury. Once he does get on the field, he will need additional time to ramp up, which means he's unlikely to be fantasy relevant until November at the earliest. The most likely outcome here is that 2026 is a down season, which is difficult timing for Charbs, considering he is entering the final year of his rookie contract. Cam Skattebo NYG | 24 Years Old Ankle Fracture-Dislocation Surgery Date: October 26, 2025 Return Timeline: Limited early in the offseason; Ready for Week 1 Skattebo's 2025 season came to an abrupt end in late October when he suffered a fractured and dislocated right ankle against the Eagles. Skattebo underwent surgery immediately after and was cleared to begin rehabbing a few weeks after the procedure. As of early January, Skattebo was out of his boot and off crutches, so he's progressing nicely. That said, he still has a long way to go in order to make a full recovery, which can take upwards of a year before players are back to full strength. Early on in the process, I'd anticipate Skattebo being pretty limited for OTAs and minicamp, but there is a chance he can be cleared at some point in training camp. Expect Skattebo's best football to be played in the back half of the season, as it may take time to regain his explosiveness and dynamic ability. Quinshon Judkins CLE | 22 Years Old Ankle Fracture-Dislocation Surgery Date: December 23, 2025 Return Timeline: Limited throughout the offseason, Likely ready for Week 1 Judkins' impressive rookie season came to a close late in the season when he suffered a right ankle fracture and dislocation. The injury is similar to that of Cam Skattebo, but the main difference here is that Judkins' injury happened about two months later. As a result, we should expect Judkins to be limited throughout the spring and summer. He's still got a chance to be cleared for Week 1, though he won't be 100% when the season begins. Generally speaking, it takes some time for players to regain their pre-injury dynamic ability, so it's likely we see Judkins get off to a slower start in 2026. He will probably be more productive over the back half of his sophomore season. Alvin Kamara NO | 31 Years Old MCL Sprain Return Timeline: Doubtful for Week 1 Kamara suffered a sprained MCL in mid August and he's now set to miss "at least a month" per multiple local and national reporters. That reporting timeline suggests the veteran is dealing with at least a Grade II (moderate) sprain. With Kamara set to miss the remainder of the preseason and training camp, he's on the wrong side of Questionable for Week 1. If this injury pushes 4-6 weeks, he'll likely miss a couple of games to begin the 2026 season. The veteran does have a history of prior knee and ankle injuries, so at this stage of his career with Etienne atop the depth chart, expect the Saints to ease him back into action once he's fully healed. Chuba Hubbard CAR | 27 Years Old Hamstring Strain Return Timeline: Week-to-week, Likely to play Week 1 News broke on August 13 that Chuba Hubbard is dealing with a hamstring injury that is considered "week-to-week" according to Dave Canales. That week-to-week prognosis does not provide much detail regarding the severity, but as we have seen across the league, hamstring injuries can linger for multiple weeks as players try to ramp up their activity level and intensity in camp. For now, I would tentatively expect Chuba to miss at least a week of practice, but it is possible he is not available until later in August. For what it's worth, Canales noted that the team does expect Chuba to be available for Week 1. Kyle Monangai CHI | 24 Years Old Hyperextended Right Knee Return Timeline: Questionable for Week 1 Chicago's RB2 left practice early on August 16 with a right knee injury and did not return. It's now being reported that Monangai suffered a hyperextension of his right knee. The expectation with this type of injury, which can include sprained ligament(s) and/or a bone bruise, is that Monangai will miss "multiple weeks." The exact details of Monangai's injury are not known, but if there is a bone bruise component to the injury, this hyperextension injury could affect his Week 1 availability. If the injury is only a mild sprain, he could get back to practice at some point in late August. Regardless of whether or not he plays in Week 1, we can expect his workload to be managed early in the season, especially after he missed time early in camp with a soft tissue injury. Isiah Pacheco DET | 27 Years Old MCL Sprain Return Timeline: Likely Available for Week 1 Dan Campbell announced on August 10 that Pacheco is expected to miss multiple weeks while recovering from a sprained MCL. He also noted that the team does expect Pacheco to return for Week 1. Assuming that is accurate, it suggests this is a mild to moderate (Grade I or Grade II) sprain, and these lower-grade MCL sprains heal well because of their great blood supply. At the time of injury, Pacheco will have roughly one month to rehab ahead of Week 1, which should be enough time for him to get back to 100% ahead of Week 1. Josh Jacobs GB | 28 Years Old Groin Strain Return Timeline: 2-3 Weeks Josh Jacobs began missing practice on August 6 with a groin injury, and as of this writing, he has yet to return to the practice field. Multiple beat reporters have suggested that the injury is not believed to be serious or long-term, but on August 11, Matt LaFleur confirmed that Jacobs is expected to miss at least one more week of practice. For now, this is a soft tissue injury that is worth monitoring, but Jacobs' Week 1 availability is not in doubt. Green Bay has historically been conservative when it comes to managing injuries, so Jacobs will likely be limited initially when he does return to the field. Bucky Irving TB | 24 Years Old Labrum Repair Surgery Date: February 2026 Return Timeline: Cleared for Week 1 Bucky Irving dealt with foot and shoulder injuries in 2025, limiting him to just 10 games. His foot injury healed without requiring surgery, but his shoulder injury did require a stabilization procedure. Reports from last year suggest that Irving's shoulder injury was a subluxation (AKA partial dislocation). These injuries require surgery in football players given the nature of the contact sport. That procedure is usually a labrum repair to help stabilize the joint. This recovery is generally straight forward, but it takes multiple months before players are cleared for contact. He didn't participate fully in OTAs or mini-camp, but he should be fully cleared for Week 1. J.K. Dobbins DEN | 27 Years Old Lisfranc Surgery Surgery Date: November 2025 Return Timeline: Limited in OTAs and Mini Camp, Cleared for Week 1 JK Dobbins suffered yet another season-ending injury in 2025. In Week 10 against the Raiders, Dobbins suffered a left mid-foot injury, likely a Lisfranc injury. Generally speaking, these injuries can be difficult for skill players in the NFL because the ligaments involved at these joints are crucial for stability in the foot during sprinting, cutting and change of direction. Initially, there was hope that Dobbins could rehab the foot without surgery and potentially return later in the season, which tells us that the injury was on the more mild side of the spectrum when it comes to Lisfranc injuries. These types of injuries range from a mild sprain (partial ligament tear) to a full dislocation of the joint with associated fracture. For Dobbins, the good news is that because his injury was on the more modest side of that spectrum, he's far more likely to return to form than a player who had suffered a more severe injury. Regardless, research does show that players coming off this procedure in Year 1 do tend to have less efficiency and reduced explosiveness upon return to play. With Dobbins having 10 months to be cleared for Week 1, I do anticipate he'll be able to enter Week 1 with minimal limitations, but he could require some time to regain his explosiveness and dynamic cutting ability. Dobbins was already participating in individual drills at OTAs, which is obviously a great sign, and he's been a full participant in training camp. RJ Harvey DEN | 25 Years Old Shoulder Labrum Repair Surgery Date: Late January/Early February 2026 Return Timeline: Training Camp News broke in mid June during OTAs that last year's rookie RB, RJ Harvey, tore the labrum in his shoulder against the Patriots in the AFC Championship game. He required surgery to repair the labrum, but the exact date of that procedure isn't known as of this writing. If we assume he had surgery shortly after the injury happened, he'll have roughly seven months before the start of Week 1. The recovery timeline here in contact sports is generally longer in an effort to protect the repair and reduce risk of re-injury. Because of that, Harvey was limited to individual drills early in training camp, but drafters can expect him to be fully cleared towards the back half of the camp and be ready for Week 1. Chris Rodriguez Jr. JAX | 25 Years Old Foot Surgery Surgery Date: Spring 2026 Return Timeline: Training Camp The Jaguars signed Chris Rodriquez Jr. in free agency, but he did not participate in OTAs or Mini Camp because of an unspecified foot injury. The injury reportedly required a procedure, but like the injury, the details of the surgery are not available as of early June. Rodriguez has been participating in individual drills in training camp as of late July/early August, and in mid August, he began participating in 11-on-11 team drills. That's a great first step in his return to the field, but it's still going to take some time for him to ramp up throughout the rest of August. Barring any setbacks, I do expect him to be ready for Week 1. Joe Mixon FA | 30 Years Old Right Ankle and Foot Injuries Surgery Date: Unknown Return Timeline: TBD Joe Mixon missed time in 2024 due to a high ankle sprain in his left leg, then missed the entire 2025 season due to an unspecified right ankle/foot injury that he suffered while training in the spring away from the facility. Speaking after the conclusion of the season, Texans GM Nick Caserio said, “It was a freak thing. Honestly, I’ve never seen it, the condition.” Caserio also added that there is nothing irresponsible that Mixon did, and that it was a medical situation that didn’t improve. Obviously, this is a murky situation and nearly impossible to speak to without knowing the specifics. Entering the 2026 offseason, it remains to be seen if the RB stays with Houston. If the team performs a physical and decides to move on, it could tell us that his foot is not in a place where the team feels comfortable to continue with him on the roster. The veteran back turned 30 in July, and after missing an entire season because of injury, it obviously brings into question Mixon's future in the NFL. Given this chronic injury, it's possible Mixon never returns to his pre-injury level of play or returns to the NFL at all. This remains an ongoing situation to monitor throughout the offseason. Najee Harris NYG | 28 Years Old Achilles Surgery Date: Late September 2025 Return Timeline: Limited throughout the offseason, Cleared for Week 1 It feels like forever ago at this point, but Harris was in the news almost daily throughout August as we awaited his return to the field following a fireworks eye injury sustained on the 4th of July. Once he was finally able to ramp up and contribute to the Chargers' offense, it looked like we were heading for a potential split with then-rookie Omarion Hampton. Unfortunately, Najee's 2025 quickly went from bad to worse in Week 3 when he tore the Achilles in his left leg against the Broncos. Harris underwent surgery the week of September 22 to repair the torn tendon. When the NFL season kicks off, he will be just under one year removed from surgery, which means he will have a good chance to be cleared for the start of the season. That said, he's unlikely to be 100% right away coming off this injury. On top of the injury recovery, Najee didn't sign until late in the season, so he didn't have a traditional NFL offseason/training camp. It'll take time for him to ramp up early in the season as he mixes in behind Cam Skattebo and/or Tyrone Tracy. Jordyn Tyson NO | 22 Years Old Hamstring Strain Return Timeline: Likely to miss 3+ regular season games; Could begin season on IR Jordyn Tyson entered the NFL with a history of hamstring injuries, and unfortunately, that trend has continued in training camp. Tyson missed games during his final year in college because of recurring hamstring problems, and the Saints tried to limit his reps in the spring in order to mitigate short term risk. While Tyson did enter camp without restrictions, he injured his hamstring again in joint practices on August 13. The Saints have said the newest injury is not related to his previous injury, yet at the same time, it's been confirmed that the rookie is seeking multiple opinions, which is not the norm for the vast majority of hamstring injuries. This suggests the injury severe enough for New Orleans to consult multiple medical professionals. When speaking about the injury, head coach Kellen Moore said "I think my understanding of this one, any player that was put in his situation where your foot slips and you get shoved from behind...Any player in that situation probably has the same diagnosis coming out of this." With Moore suggesting Tyson's foot slipped and he was shoved from behind, it's likely that this hamstring injury is located higher up towards the attachment at the hip. These proximal hamstring injuries that include the hamstring tendon do take longer to heal than most injuries in the middle of the muscle. If this is in fact what's happening with Tyson, he's going to miss multiple regular season games. Expect New Orleans to be ultra conservative with their top-10 pick after he's dealt with recurring hamstring problems for the better part of the last calendar year. He could begin the season on the IR and miss the first month of the season. Ricky Pearsall SF | 25 Years Old PCL Reconstruction Surgery Date: August 2026 Return Timeline: Will miss entire 2026 season Ricky Pearsall will undergo season-ending knee surgery. In the early days of training camp this year, he dealt with swelling in his knee related to his 2025 PCL injury. Pearsall injured his right knee in Week 4 of last year and went on to miss Weeks 5-10 because of a sprained PCL. Videos surfaced of Pearsall working out this summer with a compression sleeve on that right knee, so it is possible that Pearsall has been managing this for some time. These PCL injuries (depending on the severity) do tend to linger, and while most can be rehabbed, some do end up requiring surgery if the athlete continues to experience swelling, pain and/or instability. That PCL reconstruction surgery usually carries a 9-12 month recovery. Given that Pearsall will have his procedure in early August, he should enter 2027 with minimal restrictions, but dynasty managers can expect him to be limited in the early portion of next year's offseason program. Malik Nabers NYG | 23 Years Old ACL + Meniscus Surgery Date: October 28, 2025 Return Timeline: Limited in Training Camp, Questionable for Week 1 Nabers suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 4 against the Chargers, tearing the ACL in his right knee. It was later revealed that the talented WR also suffered additional damage to the meniscus, which has implications for his short-term recovery. In the long run, getting that structure repaired is beneficial for the health of the knee, but it will make his recovery in 2026 more cumbersome. Nabers underwent surgery in late October, just before Halloween, giving him less than one year of rehab before the start of the regular season. Generally speaking, most elite athletes recovering from an isolated ACL injury can return to the field in roughly 9-10 months. With the extra rehab time required to account for the meniscus, that timeline is usually pushed back 6-8 weeks. Because of that, Nabers is uncertain for Week 1, and there is an outside chance he could begin the regular season on PUP, especially after he required a second "clean up" procedure in the spring. He will be limited throughout the majority of training camp, but the good news is that Nabers was participating in individual drills in late July. Look for Nabers to ramp up slowly throughout August as he regains confidence in the knee. If the Giants believe he can play before Week 4, he's likely to avoid beginning the season on PUP. Look for Nabers to return closer to his pre-injury level of play in the back half of 2026 and really bounce back in a big way in 2027. Rashee Rice KC | 26 Years Old Right Knee "Clean up" Procedure Surgery Date: May 2026 Return Timeline: Likely limited to begin Training Camp; Cleared for Week 1 Rashee Rice's 2024 season came to an early end when he suffered a season-ending right knee injury. That injury included a torn lateral collateral ligament (LCL) and damage to the postero-lateral corner (PLC) and hamstring tendon. After rehabbing throughout the 2025 offseason, Rice returned to full strength last year and was productive when on the field. However, news broke in mid-May that Rice required a "clean up" procedure on his surgically repaired right knee in order to remove "loose debris." While this isolated procedure doesn't require a lengthy rehab, it does add some volatility to Rice's short and long-term outlook. PLC injuries can be complex, and it is not uncommon for these types of injuries to also include some sort of cartilage damage. The fact that Rice required a second follow-up procedure to remove loose bodies suggests this is probably the case for the Kansas City WR. I do ultimately expect him to be limited to begin training camp, but he should be cleared for Week 1. The key here is whether or not this secondary procedure helps relieve the knee irritation that had been bothering him recently. There is also a second layer to this whole story in that Rice rehabbed while in jail as he served a 30-day sentence shortly after having this second procedure. All in all, Rice is likely to be okay for the 2026 season, but the cartilage injury makes it possible that this isn't the last time we hear about knee problems in the future. Alec Pierce IND | 26 Years Old Left Ankle Surgery Surgery Date: Spring 2026 (Exact date unknown) Return Timeline: Limited to begin camp; Likely ready for Week 1 Alec Pierce is coming off a career year in 2025 and is back with the Colts after signing a massive deal in free agency. Indy is certainly counting on him to take a step forward as the leader of the offense with Michael Pittman Jr. now in Pittsburgh. While it is still possible for Pierce to regain his form this season, it wouldn't be surprising to see him get off to a slower start as he's recovering from an ankle procedure in the spring. As of this writing, the specifics of that surgery aren't known, but Pierce was seen at Colts OTAs with a sleeve on his left calf while observing practice. In that video, his left calf appears to be atrophied, and his ankle range of motion appears limited. With this new information available, Pierce will be limited to being training camp as he regains full strength and explosiveness off that left leg. Given that Pierce's offseason participation will be cut short, he could get off to a slower start in 2026, especially with his QB recovering from Achilles surgery. On July 27, the Colts placed Pierce on the PUP list to begin camp and as of August 10, he is yet to return to practice. Emeka Egbuka TB | 23 Years Old Turf Toe Return Timeline: Situation to Monitor; Questionable for Week 1 Emeka Egbuka left practice on Wednesday, August 12, with what is being described as a toe sprain after getting rolled up on at joint practices. The exact details of the injury aren't known, but the most likely outcome here is a turf toe type of injury, with multiple local beat reporters suggesting the WR will have an MRI to further evaluate the injury. For now, we will await more details on imaging for Tampa's WR1. If this is on the more mild side, Egbuka could return in 1-2 weeks. A moderate sprain could sideline him for multiple weeks and limit him into late August/early September and put his Week 1 status in jeopardy. Regardless, expect the Bucs to be conservative here in an effort to avoid this injury lingering into the regular season. Makai Lemon PHI | 22 Years Old Hamstring Strain Return Timeline: Limited throughout Training Camp, Questionable for Week 1 The Eagles' first round pick, Makai Lemon, originally injured his hamstring in the spring, forcing him to miss a portion of the team's offseason program. Unfortunately, he's dealing with a second hamstring injury in training camp, which has forced him to miss the majority of team practices through the first two weeks. The team has not provided specific details on the severity of the injury, but given his hamstring injury from spring, I'd expect the team to be cautious throughout camp and the preseason. There's no indication from the team that he'll miss regular season games, but it's reasonable to expect the rookie to get off to a slow start. He returned to practice on August 20. Luther Burden III CHI | 22 Years Old Groin Strain Return Timeline: Questionable for Week 1 Luther Burden left Bears' practice on Saturday, August 8 with a groin injury and did not return. Upon further testing, he is expected to miss the entirety of the preseason, but multiple reports indicate that the team is hopeful he's available for Week 1. Based on that timeline, this is likely a Grade II muscle strain, which carries a recovery timeline of about 4-6 weeks. With Burden missing the majority of training camp, he could be eased into regular season action, but barring a setback, this injury isn't likely to linger beyond September. For now, Burden should be considered Questionable for Week 1. Chris Brazzell II CAR | 22 Years Old LCL Sprain Surgery Date: Early August 2026 Return Timeline: Out for the year Carolina's rookie WR, Chris Brazzell, injured his knee in the first few days of training camp. On July 29, he suffered an LCL injury that was initially described as a "moderate" injury that could force him to be sidelined for 6-8 weeks. However, after further tests and evaluation, the team opted to shut him down for the year. He'll undergo surgery on his LCL and be out for the season. It's obviously not ideal to miss his entire rookie season, but this early surgery will allow him to be ready for next year's off-season program. For those with Brazzell in dynasty formats, the recovery here is generally pretty straightforward with good post-surgical results, so he should be able to enter 2027 without limitations. Chris Bell MIA | 22 Years Old ACL Surgery Date: December 2025 Return Timeline: Limited in Training Camp; Could be cleared for Week 1 Chris Bell is a rookie WR out of Louisville who was taken by the Miami Dolphins in the NFL Draft. Some draft analysts suggested that Bell was a late Round 1 talent, but he fell a bit in the draft due to his recovery from a torn ACL. During his final year in school, Bell tore the ACL in his left knee in late November of 2025 and underwent surgery in December. Reportedly, his injury was a clean ACL tear, so the recovery process here should be somewhat straightforward, with Bell likely returning to the field in roughly nine months. That gives him a chance to be cleared for the start of the season, but it is important to understand that Bell will be limited throughout the entirety of the offseason, including training camp after he was placed on the NFI list in late July. Bell was activated off NFI on August 17 and returned to practice on August 24. Even so, for a rookie looking to make the jump from college to the pros, that recovery adds an extra layer to his projection for the 2026 season. Because of the timeline and jump in level of competition, it would be surprising for Bell to make a big impact in Year 1. For dynasty managers, the most likely scenario here is that Bell is a factor in Year 2 when he is a full season removed from his injury. Tyreek Hill FA | 32 Years Old Partial Knee Dislocation Surgery Date: September 30, 2025 Return Timeline: May not play in 2026 Hill's 2025 season came to an abrupt end in Week 4 against the Jets when he suffered a serious left knee injury. During the play, Hill suffered damage to multiple ligaments, cartilage, and surrounding tissues. Unfortunately, this is a 'Tank Dell' type of injury that is going to require at least a year of rehab and recovery, if not longer. One additional concern with this type of dislocation is potential damage to the nerve that wraps around the outside of the knee. All in all, Hill is highly unlikely to be fantasy-relevant at any point in the 2026 season and may not play at all, depending on how his recovery goes. Now 32 years old, Hill's NFL future hangs in the balance, as this injury has the potential to be career-threatening. Calvin Ridley TEN | 31 Years Old Fractured Fibula Surgery Date: Mid November, 2025 Return Timeline: Cleared for Training Camp Ridley's 2025 season was defined by one thing: injury. He missed Weeks 7-9 with a hamstring injury, and upon returning to the field in Week 11 after the bye, he suffered a season-ending ankle injury. Ridley fractured the fibula in his right ankle on November 16 and underwent surgery a few days after. The good news here for Ridley is that this recovery is generally pretty straightforward and is unlikely to be a factor in 2026. He is going to be limited in the early part of the offseason as he ramps up, but he will enter training camp without any restrictions. Travis Hunter JAX | 23 Years Old LCL Surgery Date: November 11, 2025 Return Timeline: Cleared for Training Camp Hunter's rookie season was cut short due to an unfortunate season-ending knee injury that he actually suffered in practice coming out of the bye week.
